skill.name: to-issues
skill.description: Break a plan, spec, or PRD into independently-grabbable issues on the project issue tracker using tracer-bullet vertical slices.
skill.summary: Turn approved engineering plans into independent, dependency-aware issue tracker work.
skill.author: mattpocock

content.value_statement: Large plans are difficult to divide into independent engineering work. This skill creates approved vertical-slice issues with dependencies, acceptance criteria, labels, and tracker links.
actual_capabilities: Uses plans, specifications, PRDs, or referenced tracker issues as source material.
Reads referenced issue bodies and comments when issue tracker access is available.
Explores the codebase for domain vocabulary, architecture decisions, and useful prefactoring.
Creates vertical slices or expand-contract sequences for wide refactors.
Presents titles, dependencies, and covered user stories for approval.
Publishes approved issues in dependency order with labels, parent links, and blocking relationships.
limitations: Requires configured issue tracker access and the project label vocabulary.
Requires user approval before publishing the proposed issue breakdown.
Does not close or modify the source parent issue.
Avoids specific file paths and code snippets unless existing prototype code provides essential context.

use_cases.title: Convert a PRD into backlog work
use_cases.description: Split a product requirement into complete engineering slices with acceptance criteria and explicit dependencies.

use_cases.title: Plan a wide refactor
use_cases.description: Create an expand-contract sequence that keeps migration batches ordered and verifiable.

use_cases.title: Prepare work for independent agents
use_cases.description: Publish approved issues with enough context, labels, and relationships for separate implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Split a simple plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this plan into proposed issues: [plan]. Show titles, dependencies, and covered user stories. Do not publish until I approve.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start with a short plan that needs a clear issue breakdown.

prompt_templates.title: Decompose an existing issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Review issue [reference], including its comments. Propose vertical-slice issues using our domain vocabulary and ADRs. Ask for approval before publishing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use an issue tracker item as the source for implementation work.

prompt_templates.title: Sequence a wide refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this wide refactor into an expand-contract issue sequence: [refactor]. Keep each migration batch verifiable and list every blocking relationship. Wait for approval.
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan a mechanical change that affects many packages or call sites.

prompt_templates.title: Publish a complete delivery plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [plan or PRD] against the current codebase. Identify prefactoring, vertical slices, labels, parent links, and native blocking edges. Publish blockers first after approval.
prompt_templates.scenario: Create and publish a dependency-aware issue set for a complex project.

output_examples.input: Split a passwordless sign-in PRD into issues.
output: Store one-time sign-in challenges. Blocked by: None.
Complete email-link sign-in. Blocked by: challenge storage.
Add sign-in audit events. Blocked by: email-link sign-in.

output_examples.input: Plan a shared account identifier rename across four packages.
output: Expand: add the new identifier beside the old one.
Migrate: create one issue for each package, all blocked by Expand.
Contract: remove the old identifier after every migration issue.

best_practices: Provide the full plan, success criteria, tracker details, and label vocabulary.
Review slice granularity and dependency links before approving publication.
Use vertical slices for features and expand-contract sequencing for wide refactors.
anti_patterns: Do not publish issues before the proposed breakdown receives approval.
Do not split work only by schema, API, UI, or test layers.
Do not include fragile implementation paths when behavior and acceptance criteria are sufficient.

faq.question: What source material can I provide?
faq.answer: You can provide a plan, specification, PRD, issue number, tracker URL, or issue path.

faq.question: Does the skill publish issues immediately?
faq.answer: No. It presents the breakdown, asks about granularity and dependencies, and waits for approval.

faq.question: How does it handle dependencies?
faq.answer: It publishes blockers first, then adds native blocking edges or fallback references in issue bodies.

faq.question: Can it handle large refactors?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses expand-contract sequencing with separate expansion, migration, contraction, and optional integration issues.

faq.question: Will it modify the parent issue?
faq.answer: No. The instructions explicitly prohibit closing or modifying any parent issue.

faq.question: What tracker setup is required?
faq.answer: The agent needs tracker access and the project triage label vocabulary before publishing.
